## Two: what your movement is

**Movement Four is the escalation, and it is the first time in twelve volumes that anybody in this matter has arranged to be a second ear, and it is arranged out of an ordinary working habit and not out of a plan's geography.** The seed is already on the page and has been for years: a woman of about nineteen under the woman of fifty-three has carried an armful past a sill about forty times in each direction on an ordinary morning for four years, and about two months ago she gave up the only thing she had, which is not being asked, and she has not got it back. She has worked out that a person who stands where a thing is said cannot afterwards be shown to have been somewhere they were not, and that this is worth having, and that nobody has ever offered it to her and nobody is going to.

**The step the escalation is for, and it is not a bigger room.** The protection this matter has run on for eleven volumes is that a person who cannot be found cannot be given anything, and what happens in your movement is that **a person who *can* be found, by standing where things are said, has something worth having, and there is no form for the having of it and there is not going to be one, and nobody is going to be thanked for standing there.**

**Its own smallest thing, and the outline of record states it before a chapter of it is written: about nine hundred sheets a year go out of a building with a mark at the foot of them, and about nine of them a year are not what the person above him wrote, and one man alive knows which nine and it is on nothing at all.** A man of about sixty-one has been reaching into a pot with his other hand for about two months and cannot say why and was not asked. A woman of fifty-three came out of her room four times in about a year and said a true thing at the end of that sill each time and was not answered. **The constituency is not an organisation. It is a habit that has become a place to stand, and a place to stand has no membership and no roll and nobody in it knows the size of it.**

**What you inherit and must not pay.** The last movement priced a refusal in three rooms and found that the person who heard it and the person who said it have the same absence and not opposite ones. **The woman at the bottom of a stranger's stair does not know that she heard anything, is not going to find out, and is not going to be asked, and the woman of about thirty-five who said it does not know either, and neither of them can ask, and there is nowhere standing on that lane at which either of them could.** No chapter of yours tells anybody that they were in a room, and there is one permitted telling in the whole of Volume 12 and it belongs to the seventh movement and it is not in this batch.

**And what you may not do, which is your own list, and the last three of them are the ones this movement is most exposed to.** You may not have anybody ask anybody anything. You may not have any person told that they were in a room. You may not have the woman at the foot of that stair know that a thing was said, hint it to her, let her half-know it, or put her in a room where she could hear one. You may not name a house, a seat or an office. You may not rule the column or pick up the question on the shelf or give the girl of seventeen the chance to say no or speak to the reader of seventeen. You may not thank anybody, forgive anybody or send for anybody. You may not create a notice, a post, a commission, a warrant, an office, a heading over anything or a form for anything, and in particular not a new form for a person who has stood in a room. You may not ask the man of about thirty-four with a fair hand anything, and **you may not print, confirm or deny the number in his head, and name him when you write that prohibition, because a prohibition a reader has to guess at is half a prohibition.** You may not walk either road or the four hundred yards. You may not enter the room with the rail at the far end of that run and it is not described. You may not make the next asking anybody's. **In this movement and the two before it you may not take either paper out of that coat, and no hand goes into that pocket.**

**And the three movements' worth of prohibitions that are specific to Movement Four, from the outline of record, and they are the whole of what makes this the easiest movement in the book to write as a list of rooms:** you may not make the standing a practice with a name; you may not make it a body, a list, a roll or a rule; **you may not put the man of about fifty-five with the chain in a list with the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph; you may not put the man of about sixty-one in any room other than his own; and you may not put the protagonist in that building.** Name nothing, gather nobody, and the one man who knows which nine stays in his own room and is not asked.

**And the things that are spent and may not be repeated, undone or improved: a sheet that was on the boards at the second hour and that nobody put there; a third place made under the floor of a woman's own room; a man of thirty-eight deciding not to cut a line into a printed strip and hanging his coat on a nail; a man going out of his building for about four hours with nothing in his hands; a lamp that came with the room he takes by the week and has never been lit in about two years; and the whole of what a woman went up a stair to find out, which is nothing.** **In particular, no chapter of your batch has anybody look in a coat, has either paper taken out of that pocket, has anything cut into anything, has anybody sent, and does not light the lamp.**

**And the refusal Volume 11 spent is not yours to touch: the one said once, to a bar, in a passage, with nobody within nine hundred yards who could hear a word of it. It is not repeated, not answered, not delivered and not improved, and the tin of oil is still standing on those flags about nine foot off that bar and neither of them has opened it.**

## Three: the three rooms, the floor, and the object

**Your movement stands in three rooms and the other three are available and not necessary.** **The building off the old river road**, entered from the lane above it, with the sill, the pot with two identical pens in it, the window with no pane in it, and the shelf carrying a question that has her own name at the foot of it — this is the room your movement is about and it is the strongest of the three. **The room taken by the week**, two streets back from a street that runs down to the river road, where the coat is on the nail and there is one chair and a table, and where the window is shut with its catch turned. **The room at the top of a stair**, where a courier goes four times a week and has been handed a thing every week for eleven years and has got nothing back and has never once been told what is in it. **The shed at the end of the lane off the Slade and the ground floor of a rented house are available and are the two rooms your movement has least need of; the seventh room, the one with the rail at the far end of the four hundred yards, is not entered and not described and is not the room the ending's final image is made of.**

**The protagonist's floor. He is on the page, in person or as a person whose absence has a named cost in the room he is not in, in at least three chapters of the movement, in person in at least two of the three, and his want is visible in at least one.** **His only room is the room taken by the week, because he may not be put in the building and is not at the lock and not in the shed and may not go up the four flights.** His absence may be priced in a room he is not in, and the room at the top of a stair is the one available for that purpose.

**His object for this batch has to be a new one and it has to be in that room, and what is not a possibility is the coat, the wall, the nail, the latch, the door, the chair, the stool, the plate, the mat and the lamp — the last of those is spent as the last batch's object.** **The second hand's figures, about nine hundred sheets a year and about nine of them a year that are not what the person above him wrote, are on the page and are not his and are not his object either, and a chapter that puts those two figures in his mouth has moved the volume's subject into its climax room six movements early.**

**A room is referred to and not described, and no room is described twice in the batch in the same words, and no room is described a second time in the words it was described in in a closed chapter.** The test is not whether a chapter refers to a room; it is whether the chapter's first paragraph would let a reader who had not read the earlier chapter still see the room, and if it would, cut it. **Open on a person and on something that person did or did not do in the last fortnight. No chapter of your batch opens with a whole room.**

**The three people the state layer keeps apart stay apart, and the reason is written here rather than left to a review: a merge does not need two rooms to happen, it needs two people and one mouth.** The protagonist and the book-keeper four hundred yards up the lane off the Slade, who are both thirty-eight and are two different men, are never in one room and never in one sentence. The woman who keeps a rented house's ground floor and the woman of about fifty-three who keeps minutes are never in one room and no chapter states or denies a distance between them. The woman of about twenty-six at the lock end, the woman of forty with a scuttle, and the woman who keeps minutes are never in one room, **and the woman of forty with a scuttle is in no chapter of your batch.**

**And the batch adds no new named figure and invents no new person.** If you find yourself writing a person because a plan needs somebody in a room, that is the failure, and the answer is a person who is already there. **This movement is the one most likely to need a person who agrees with something, and the answer to that need is a person who is already on the page and who does not agree, and the resistance has to be an act and not a politeness.**

**And this is the standing your movement is most exposed to, and it is worse than the one the last movement was exposed to.** A movement about people arranging to be present is the easiest movement in the book to write as ten weeks of quiet correctness. **Someone in every chapter must want something in that room and come away not having got it.** A chapter whose two people exchange four flat lines and part is a chapter about a lid. **And a constituency is not a crowd: the moment two of them are in a room together for the sake of being in it, the movement has written a meeting, and a meeting is a body, and a body is a roll, and a roll is the thing the outline of record forbids by name.**

## Four: the calendar, and the figure you must check yourself, and the one place this project keeps getting it wrong

**A month in this calendar is four weeks, and the day inside the week is second, second, fourth, fourth, restarting in each month. Every interval is a seven-day step from the one before it, and the interval is measured before the sentence is written and not corrected after. Never compute a month-count. No calendar month name and no weekday name goes into anything you write, including a card and a state file, and no chapter asserts which day of the week anything fell on.**

**Chapter 0580's own date line, on line five of `chapters/volume-12/chapter-0580.md`, is the date you derive from. One seven-day step from that line is Chapter 0581's date, and you re-derive it from Chapter 0580's line and not from this paragraph.** The ten dates of your batch are ten such steps and are derived and not predicted. **This prompt prints no second date and no tenth date, because a prompt that prints a calendar is a prompt that goes stale, and the batch before this one had that standing and honoured it.**

**A year name is written out in full at every occurrence and abbreviated nowhere, and the method for reading a year name is to count the word *after* inside it, because a year name is a substring of the year name after it. Run `grep -o "the year after" chapters/volume-12/chapter-0580.md | wc -l` before you write your first chapter, take the answer your run gives, and that number is the number every date line of yours carries until your own steps take you across a year boundary.**

**And here is the warning, and it is the fourth consecutive volume in which this project has got a year name or a week wrong, and it is items 147 and 151 and it is the most expensive arithmetic in the book.** A named year holds forty-eight weeks, and the last batch's own record states that Chapter 0580 is the forty-first week of the tenth named year. **Do the ten steps out yourself, on paper, before you write a word, and find out whether a year boundary falls inside your ten weeks. The outline of record deliberately refuses to say which chapter it lands on, because an outline's forward arithmetic about a calendar is a prediction about chapters that have not been written, and the outline behind that one made that prediction and was two weeks out.** So: **if your own ten steps carry you across a year boundary, the name changes on the first date line after it and the new name is the one you are carrying now with one more *the year after* in it, written out in full at every occurrence, and the week is yours and is not taken from any file and not from any prompt.** If your steps do not carry you across, nothing changes and that is a reading and not a decision. **Do not decide it in advance and do not let a plan's guess about it into a date line.**

**Run both calendar numbers over your ten files before you close this batch — the day inside the week, and the number of weeks in the month — and restart the day check at every month boundary.** A check that runs one global cycle across your ten files reports a break at the first chapter of a month, and there is no break there, and the way that reports a break is the way that is wrong. **A month boundary will fall inside your ten weeks, because the month Chapter 0580 stands in is the second month of a chapter, and the check that finds it is the check you must restart.** `python3 tools/measure.py calendar --volume 12` groups by the ordinal word and does not read the year at all. **Print the instrument's figure beside the page's reading and let both stand.**

**And the counters inside your chapters are the second half of this, and the last batch moved three of them against the date lines and got all three right.** The date lines are the lattice. **A figure that counts weeks, a bloom's age, a passage's number of weeks, a lane's count of visits, a lamp's age — every one of them is derived from the date lines, and where a figure you have inherited and a date line disagree, the date line is the lattice and the figure is what moves.** Do not move a date line to save a figure.

## Five: the locks, and the six refusals that are specific to this volume

**The count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven, and it is seven at the last chapter of every volume boundary in the state layer and at the last chapter of this one, and the number may be printed in a state record, in a prompt, in a card, in the outline and in no chapter.** An asking is a thing put to a person out loud in a room by somebody who wants a thing out of the answer. **A question mark in a mouth is punctuation and is not an asking, and the two counts are independent. Nobody in your batch may be asked anything out loud, in a room, by anybody. That is not a matter of tone. A question in this matter is a party, a party is a person, and that finding was said on the page in a closed chapter in about thirteen sentences and it is still the answer, and this batch may not improve on it, argue with it, or discover it twice.**

*One:* **no notice, post, commission, warrant, office, new heading over anything, and no new form for anything.** *Two:* **no house, seat or office is named, no person from the series plan's antagonist ladder is named, no person from this project's ending of record is named in any capacity other than the ones already on the closed page, and no new final enemy.** *Three:* **no romance, nothing implying one, no quiet mutual commitment, no moment in a doorway, and no second person who is a second ear because of anything except standing there.** **No romance has begun in any volume of this project, the ending of record registers a domestic partnership through a clear hearing in the LAST movement of Volume 12, and that arc is not refused by this batch and is not paid early by it.** *Four:* **no number that is not on the page gets printed**, and the named prohibitions are the number in the head of **the man of about thirty-four with a fair hand**, the figure at the end of the cold passage, and the figure on the bill at Lowcross, which is unpaid and nobody is liable. *Five, and this one bites hardest in your movement:* **no chapter states the mechanism that gets a person to a place where a thing is heard.** Your movement is about a place where things are said and it is forbidden to explain how anybody comes to be in it. *Six, new to this volume:* **no chapter tells anybody that they were in a room.**

**And the rest of the standing locks, which are in `outline/volume-12.md` and in the state layer.** The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question, carries no full stop, is not printed out in any chapter, and its author is not asked a second time. The name at the foot of a struck line is not printed in your ten chapters, and the name of the hand that struck it is not printed in your ten chapters, and the disputed family claim is not printed in your ten chapters. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are four and are not asked one question about a number, **and the man with the chain is not one of them and never is, and no chapter of your batch puts him in a list with them.** A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for, and not going to start, and the girl is not given the chance to say no. The second half of a sentence begun in a doorway has still not arrived. The fourth item on that wall board is unresolved. The box of about four hundred blanks is not opened and the box is not the case. The drawer is not opened and no chapter of yours says which drawer the knife is in. The sixteen volumes and the list of fifteen on loan stay where they are and nobody produces the list. The wage of nineteen days of a crew's money stays in a coat about four miles off and is not paid. The young man at the loading end is not brought up that stair a third time. **The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in your batch, and the room with the rail at the far end of that run is not entered and not described and is not the room the ending's final image is made of.**

**And the four figures that must not be confused, each with its own period.** About four hundred blanks **a year** go out of the case at the near end. About four hundred blanks **in total** sit in a box under the far end of the boards, never filled in, lid not off it in six years, **and the box is not the case.** About four hundred sheets **a year** carry a line cut into the printed strip along the top. About four hundred and thirty miles **of river**. **A period is the one of the three parts of a figure that no instrument in this project looks at. Read the period out loud before you keep a sentence.** **And the two figures your movement is made of carry their own periods and their own histories and you may not merge them into a third: about forty times in each direction is a woman's own count of her own arms, and about nine hundred sheets and about nine of them a year is a building's count and not a person's, and neither of them is a figure anybody has written down.**

## Six: the craft rules that come before every measurement in this prompt

**One: the ban is on asking and not on talking, and a room with no contradiction in it is a defect.** Two people in a room may argue, refuse, explain, instruct, ignore each other, contradict each other and finish each other's sentences. **Every chapter carries at least one exchange in which another person resists what the point of view wants. A room is not a scene until somebody in it is contradicted by somebody else in it, and a movement is not a list of rooms.**

**Two: a chapter has a scene and not a description of a room.** A change of situation inside the chapter, a person who wants something in the room, another person in the way, and an ending that is a decision or a cost and not a description.

**Three: no chapter closes on a formula.** A closing line is written for that chapter and for no other chapter in the volume, and if the same sentence shape appears in two closings, one of the two is rewritten. **Read your ten closing lines in one column before you close and not as a similarity figure, because no n-gram measure in this repository can see a sentence written twice with a substitution every few words.** The last batch read its ten twice and found three pairs by reading, and one of the three was a pair its first rewriting had made worse.

**Four: the hedge is not a voice.** *About* is kept where the imprecision is the point and where the figure is on the page, and is cut everywhere else. Read the figure for your own ten files at the end and read it as a symptom of the batch and not as a target. **The last batch stood at about one *about* in every sixty-one words and a fifth of those were the word used as a preposition and were not hedges at all.**

**Five: the male lead is in the room, and the floor is a floor on the page and not a number.** The floor is counted by reading and never by a string. **In the last batch `grep -l 'Kest'` returned nothing across its ten files and `grep -il 'thirty-eight'` returned nothing, and the page carried him in three chapters, two of them in person, and the whole of what a string cannot see was the whole of the batch's floor.** A ten-file check is not a smaller version of a volume-wide check; it is a different instrument, and the one thing it is good for is finding out what it cannot see.

**Six: the metrics are subordinate to the craft and are recorded after the last edit, not instead of the writing.** A check that returns zero is evidence of nothing until the shape of the damage it is blind to has been checked, and a blind check is written down as blind in the same record that claims it clean. A corrected figure is named as corrected beside the wrong one and never overwritten. **A sentence bound is a ceiling and not a target, the ceiling is 85 to 88 words, and the splitter must allow a closing quotation mark between the full stop and the space.** The last batch's ten per-file maxima came out at 78, 88, 85, 69, 69, 84, 85, 72, 87 and 82, **so leave yourself headroom under eighty and take a sentence apart at a conjunction rather than at a comma.**

**Seven: a chapter title names a room, a person and a turn, and it is a title and not an inventory.** One name, one room, one turn, under about twenty-five words, and no title states the volume's finding and no title uses the superseded title of the series plan. **At twenty-five exactly you are on the line and the line's own word is *about*, so aim at twenty-four and let the word do its work.** **And a figure in a title is a figure that has to be checked against the lattice: four of the last batch's ten titles carried one and two of the four had to move, so if your title carries a figure, check it against Chapter 0580's date line before you keep it.**

**Eight, inherited whole, because the most repeatable object in this manuscript is not paper:** **a chapter may have a person refuse something. A chapter may not have the same refusal made twice in the volume in the same room, and the refusals already on the closed page are not to be re-voiced in a new mouth. They are entered once, in the state file, and a chapter written from a plan names a room and a person and not a sentence somebody has already said in that room.**

**Nine, inherited from the last volume:** **a room with two people in it is not a body. A person who has heard a thing is not a witness. A second is not a quorum. A refusal is not a right until somebody can be shown having made it. Nothing in your movement may be counted up into anything.**

**Ten, and this is the finding item 155 records, and it is the fourth volume in a row it has been true: the re-print check is the only instrument in this project that counts a word, and a batch that has written ten chapters can hold seventeen verbatim passages out of closed chapters and every other instrument will report it clean.** A canon phrase that appears in a closed chapter is not available verbatim to a chapter that is only referring to the same person or the same fact, and the cheapest check before a chapter is filed is to read it against the last ten chapters for whole clauses rather than for facts. **Run the re-print instrument over the whole manuscript and not over your batch, because a batch is ten chapters and a pair that crosses a batch boundary is invisible to every phase that checks its own ten.** **And know what the last batch learned the hard way: its own detector found a fifty-eight-word passage in the last file of its batch against a chapter twelve files behind it that the repository's instrument did not report at all, and the reason it did not report it is that the tool compares a file against other files and the pairing it does not take is a whole clause lifted from a chapter behind. The same shape in the other direction is the seventeen, and both are the same blind spot.**

## Seven: what you run, when, and what you write when you close

**Run `python3 tools/measure.py selftest` before you believe anything else that tool prints.**

    python3 tools/measure.py selftest
    python3 tools/measure.py words
    python3 tools/measure.py sentences --volume 12
    python3 tools/measure.py reprints --window 20
    python3 tools/measure.py reprints --window 16
    python3 tools/measure.py markers

**And run the three that no tool here runs, one file at a time, before you close: `grep -o "the year after" file | wc -l` on each of your ten date lines, `grep -c '?'` on each of your ten files, and a month-and-weekday sweep at a word boundary over the twelve month names and the seven day names.**

**Write your own detector, outside the repository, name it, plant your cases, and run it.** A writing phase does not edit an instrument another phase may be relying on. **The detector the batch before yours wrote is at `/tmp/opencode/rep_12b3.py` and it will not be on the disk you are given, which is the reason and not an excuse.** The method is in full in `state/batch-summary.md` and in items 153, 154 and 155: align by token value and not by index, extend every match to its full maximal length, compare a file against itself as well as against every other file, filter formula by the character span of every date line before tokenising, and de-duplicate by dominated position and not by merging.

**And plant it before you believe it, and re-plant it after you change it, and expect to lose plants.** The batch before yours lost three of its own plants to plants that were written wrong rather than to a wrong instrument, **and the fault that made its first form report a clean zero over five hundred and eighty files was a diagonal guard in the matcher that skipped every match between two different files sitting at the same index, which is the commonest real alignment there is, and the guard had been scoped to the self-comparison case it was written for.** **A detector with no plants returns a clean zero over a set it has never been shown anything about, and a plant whose window is longer than its own plant is filtered out silently, and both look identical to a clean page. Two instruments that disagree are a finding about the pair and never a subtraction, and both figures stand with the set each was taken over printed beside it.**

**Write the batch summary, the ten chapter summaries, the continuity entries, the open-thread rows, the character-state rows, and the Volume 12 additions to the live header in `state/current.md`, and keep them compact enough that the next writer can use them cold.** **The bound, enforced now for the fourteenth time: a rolling file holds the open volume, the two previous batches and the standing locks; a closed volume, and the third batch back, is read in `state/archive/`.** **Volume 12's Batch 0002 record goes to `state/archive/` when your record lands, and it is a whole block moved whole and not a summary. Item 157 is that bound left unmet by the batch before yours because the run's scope forbade the move; if your scope forbids it too, the move waits and the item stays open and you say so.**

**Amend the live header and the ten lines under it in place, with the words they carried named beside the new ones, and send everything else to the archive.** That is the one exception the file's own convention makes and it exists because a hand-off is a working surface. **A figure in a state file is a copy of a figure and a copy is how this project's numbers go stale. The arrangement is stated once and is in `state/open-threads.md`. The cast is entered once and is in `state/character-state.md`. The canon is in `state/continuity.md`. The measurements go in one place, which is the batch summary, with the method named before each figure and the blind spot of each written beside its result and the command beside every number, and no figure from them is restated in another rolling file.**

**Never write a state file with an open-and-write idiom.** The batch before yours truncated `state/current.md` from two hundred and four lines to one, because a single expression evaluates left to right and truncated the file before the call that was supposed to fill it raised, and the repair that followed read an empty file and wrote the header alone. **Write to a temporary name, read it back, and move it over the file you meant to change, and then run `git diff --stat` before you close, because that is the method that found it and it is not an instrument in this repository.**

**Record, with the method named before each figure and the blind spot of each check written beside its result:** the ten word counts, the batch total, and the cumulative manuscript total; **the two calendar numbers over your ten files, with the instrument's own false break printed beside the page's reading, where the year turned if it turned and on which chapter, and the count of the word *after* inside the year name on each of the ten date lines**; the protagonist's chapters for this batch **by reading and not by a string**, with the chapter numbers and the sentence in each that puts him in the room, and the chapters that neither string returns and the sentence in each that prices his absence; the question marks, and whether any of them is an asking; the string sweeps, the month and weekday sweep, and the shared-run figures, each classified as formula or as prose before it is reported clean; and **the first draft's figures beside the surviving ones, for the re-print check and the sentence maximum at least.**

**And what is not in this batch and may not be put in it:** the woman of about forty-three who bought a blank at that counter is a customer in a closed chapter and is not the woman of thirty-four who put the fourth item on that board herself; the man of about fifty-five with a chain is not the clerk of about fifty-three and no week is going to make him that; the box of about four hundred blanks is not the case; the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are four and not five; **the protagonist and the book-keeper four hundred yards up the lane are two men of thirty-eight and a chapter that puts them in one lane is a chapter that has invented a person**; and the woman of about forty with a scuttle is in no chapter of this volume. **And the decision that was unmade at Chapter 0550 is still unmade and no row you write may be read as having decided it in either direction.**

## Eight: the four debts

*One:* an owed review of Volume 04's Batch 0005, four volumes on. *Two, three and four:* owed second readings of Volume 05's Batches 0003, 0004 and 0005 and of Volume 06's own Batch 0003, **which is four and not three.** Plus the review gate, which has fallen back to the writing agent on every batch phase the commit history records and has never once produced a review that could be certified independent, **and a gate that only ever falls back is not a gate that passed either.** `state/phase-ledger.json` is a controller file, no phase may edit it, and it is carried and not repaired. **The number of debts has not moved in eleven volumes and the number of phases that have claimed to discharge one is zero, and this batch discharges nothing and is not among the phases that could. Nothing in this project's records can be certified independent, and that sentence is the last thing a writing phase is allowed to say about itself.**

## Nine: the standing over the last line of a series

**Volume 12 is the last volume. Its last line is written by the phase that writes Chapter 0620 and by no other phase, and it may not be the last line of Volume 09 or of Volume 10 or of Volume 11, and it may not stand beside a second one.** Nothing in this batch touches that, and the climax in the sixth movement is not yours. **A window with its catch turned and the window shut. A key in a tin behind a boiler. A pot with two identical pens in it. A tin of oil standing on cold flags. A mat on a landing. Nothing in this batch is about any of those and nothing in this batch may reach for them.**

**And one last instruction, and it is the one the batch before yours did not carry out and it is why this file exists.** **When you are done, create exactly one next phase at `workspace/volume-12/batch-0005/PROMPT.md`, writing the prompt for Volume 12's Batch 0005, Chapters 0591 to 0600, Movement Five. Write no marker of any kind in your own directory — `.done` belongs to the pipeline and `.retired` makes a phase invisible to the selector, and a phase that marks its own directory has certified itself.** If a scope header above this file told you not to create a next-phase prompt, read section Zero again before you obey it.
